findings.title: Recreate exit code silently changed from 4 to 3, and 4 now means something else
findings.body: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` changes from 4 to 3, and 4 is reused as `FEATURE_DISABLED`. Scripts or pipelines written against the previous release treat exit code 4 as "recreate upgrade required". After this change they will read 4 as recreate when the real cause is that the feature was not enabled. They will also no longer recognise the actual recreate signal (3). Reusing a code that previously had another meaning makes the mismatch silent instead of failing loudly. Either keep 4 for recreate and pick a new code for feature-disabled, or call out the change explicitly in the release and upgrade notes.

findings.title: Feature-disabled test checks neither the exit code nor the `check` subcommand
findings.body: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the error message for the `metadata` subcommand. It does not assert the new documented exit code 4 (`CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED`). It also does not exercise the same guard in `UpdateCompatibilityCheck`, which is the command whose exit code scripts rely on. A regression in either the exit code or the `check` guard would go unnoticed.

findings.title: Exit code 4 is described as "Rolling Upgrade is not possible"
findings.body: The table describes exit code 4 as "Rolling Upgrade is not possible". In reality no compatibility check is performed: the command exits immediately because the feature is not enabled. Automation that maps every non-zero, non-error code to "recreate" will choose an unnecessary downtime upgrade because of this wording. The entry should say this is a usage/configuration error and that no compatibility decision was made.

findings.title: Test overwrites any enabled features from the base test deployment
findings.body: `setEnabledFeatures(List.of(...))` replaces whatever features `getTestKeycloakDeployment` may already have enabled instead of appending `rolling-updates`. If the base deployment enables features (now or later), the RECREATE variant of this test silently runs with a different feature set than the null-strategy variant.
